questions.text: The text says batch cooking should happen on Monday.

questions.text: According to the text, what type of student manages food best?
opts: Those who eat only canteen food
questions.hint: "The students who manage best are those who accept that they'll sometimes eat too much pizza..."

questions.text: Daniyar spends about ___ tenge per month on groceries.
questions.hint: "I spend about 8,000 tenge a month on groceries."

questions.text: What is "batch cooking" according to the text?
opts: Preparing food in advance for the whole week
questions.correct: Preparing food in advance for the whole week
questions.hint: "Spend two hours on Sunday preparing food for the week."

questions.text: The text says a healthy diet means eating zero processed food.
questions.hint: "Eating well is not about perfection. It doesn't mean eating zero processed food."

questions.text: In Listening 1, how much money do Rustam and Kamila have to spend?
questions.hint: "About 4,000 tenge. Not a lot, but enough for the basics."

questions.text: In Listening 1, why does Kamila say not to buy a large bottle of oil?
questions.hint: "Don't get too much — we don't use a lot of oil."

questions.text: In Listening 2 (recipe), Rustam uses ___ grams of minced meat.
questions.hint: "400 grams of minced lamb or beef."

questions.text: In Listening 2, what happens if you add too much fat to manti?
questions.hint: "don't add too much fat or the manti become greasy."

questions.text: In Listening 2, Rustam's recipe requires two eggs in the dough.
questions.hint: "Just one. One egg and a pinch of salt."

questions.text: In Listening 1, how many bags of each vegetable does Kamila suggest?
questions.hint: "Don't buy too many. One bag of each is enough."

questions.text: "How ___ flour do you need?" (flour is uncountable)
questions.hint: "flour" = uncountable → "how MUCH flour?" ✅

questions.text: "How ___ eggs does the recipe need?" (countable)
questions.hint: "eggs" = countable → "how MANY eggs?" ✅

questions.text: "There's too ___ oil." (oil is uncountable)
questions.hint: "too much" + uncountable. "There's TOO MUCH oil." ✅

questions.text: "There are too ___ onions." (countable)
questions.hint: "too many" + countable. "There are TOO MANY onions." ✅

questions.text: "The soup isn't hot ___." (insufficient temperature)
questions.hint: adjective + enough: "isn't hot ENOUGH" = needs to be hotter. ✅

questions.text: "Add ___ salt." (small amount, recipe instruction)
questions.hint: "salt" = uncountable → "a little salt" (small positive amount). ✅

questions.text: "I have ___ rice." (large positive amount)
questions.hint: Positive + uncountable → "a lot of". "I have A LOT OF rice." ✅ (not "much" in positive)

questions.text: "There isn't ___ water left." (insufficient)
questions.hint: "not enough water" = insufficient. "There isn't ENOUGH water." ✅

questions.text: "Batch cooking" means:
opts: Cooking in advance to have food ready all week
questions.correct: Cooking in advance to have food ready all week
questions.hint: "batch cooking" = preparing a large quantity at one time to use over several days.

questions.text: "A moderate amount of carbohydrates" means:
opts: A reasonable amount — not too much or too little
questions.correct: A reasonable amount — not too much or too little
questions.hint: "moderate" = not extreme; within reasonable limits. Neither too much nor too little.

questions.text: She makes one big pot of soup to ___ cooking time — a classic batch approach.
questions.hint: "save cooking time" = batch cooking saves time during the week.

questions.text: "Nutritional value" refers to:
opts: The health benefits and nutrients food provides
questions.correct: The health benefits and nutrients food provides
questions.hint: "nutritional" = relating to nutrients. "Nutritional value" = how much goodness a food provides.

questions.text: "We've got plenty of tea." "Plenty" means:
questions.hint: "plenty of" = more than enough. "Plenty of tea" = lots of tea, no need to buy more.
